[P2] Require coverage for a single unsupported destination

The invalid-destination tests supply either zero keys or two keys, so both reject through `keys.length !== 1`. Deleting `keys[0] !== key` leaves every assertion unchanged, allowing a single unsupported provider to pass factory validation and fail later inside a durable step. This violates CONTRIBUTING rule 4. Return to the configuration/test design and require factory-time rejection of a single unsupported destination, or simplify the destination wrapper while only Bedrock is supported.
